- When sentiment is consistently negative (0.00 or low) and model forecasts remain high, reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After a sharp spike in price, model tends to overcorrect — suppress subsequent forecast increases for 3–5 days.
- If official event net is strongly bearish (net < -10) and sentiment is neutral or negative, forecast should trend downward with diminishing slope.
- When sentiment history shows early drops (e.g., 0.00 after high), model often fails to adjust — anticipate downward correction in next 5–7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from mean of last 18 days, adjust forecast mean to align with recent price action, not historical trend.
- If official events show supply net < -5 and sentiment is neutral, forecast should be 5–10% below historical mean for next 7 days.
- When sentiment history shows 0.00 for 3+ consecutive days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast amplitude by 10–20% for next 5 days.
- If model forecast is >15% above recent 18-day average and sentiment is neutral or bearish, apply downward bias of 5–10% for next 3–5 days.
